parts.text:
**Observing UI Anomalies**

I've zeroed in on the UI within `w992.png`. My attention is drawn to the teal bar; specifically, the overlay of the 4 icons (calendar, email, folder, document) and the word "Dashboard" with "Home > Main Dashboard." The top left corner needs deeper inspection as well.


**Analyzing Width Discrepancies**

I've uncovered the core issue: the `navbar-links-wrapper`'s width is set to zero for screens at or below 991px, causing the overlap. However, at 992px, the width is calculated with the sidebar dimensions, but with the `.nav-link` still set to display `none`. Thus, the links are hidden but still taking up space, creating the observed UI glitch, and I must figure out what happens when the display changes.


**Investigating CSS Transitions**

I'm now diving into the CSS transitions and media queries within the codebase. The switch from `max-width: 991px` to `@media (max-width: 991px)` seems to be causing an issue with the transition of the `navbar-menu-wrapper`. It seems the width calculation changes, leading to the overlapping elements, and I'm currently tracing the logic behind it, and I'll keep digging through the code.


**Examining HTML Structure**

I'm now inspecting the HTML structure, specifically the `navbar-breadcrumb` element. The `navbar-links-wrapper`, containing the icons, and the `navbar-menu-wrapper`, holding the "Dashboard" text, are siblings within this section, so there must be some sort of issue with relative positioning or the display. The structure's classes will be my next focus.


**Deciphering Width Calculations**

I've traced the width calculations, pinpointing the root cause. The `.navbar-menu-wrapper`'s width depends on `100%` of `.navbar-breadcrumb`'s width, from which the width of `.navbar-links-wrapper` is subtracted. That means the Dashboard text is dynamic based on this calculation, which uses the dimensions of the sidebar. I must trace the logic and figure out how the `navbar-links-wrapper`'s width is influenced by the sidebar dimensions. The padding adds another layer of complexity.


**Verifying Box Model**

I'm now confirming the box model implementation. I discovered that `.navbar-menu-wrapper` uses `box-sizing: border-box` and Bootstrap's default settings. So, the width calculation, `calc(100% - 244px)`, includes padding. The content of `.navbar-menu-wrapper` has a left-side list with a "Dashboard" header, and a right-side list containing a search input that's roughly 260px wide! The `ul.navbar-nav` has flex settings. I'm now looking at why icons overlapped with "Dashboard." I will inspect the layout of `navbar-breadcrumb` at 992px to see the window size.


**Confirming Media Query Effects**

I've just run a test at 975px which falls under the `max-width: 991px` media query. The window is 992px, but the actual available space is 975px. This confirms that the `.navbar-links-wrapper` has a width of zero, but it lacks `overflow: hidden`. The `nav-link` element is set to `display: none` within the same media query, but the links do not disappear until 992. I'm focused on resolving why the elements overlap despite the width adjustment to `0`.

**Analyzing Window Sizes**

I'm now focusing on a specific instance, `w992.png`. It's strange this screenshot had icons, so I'm investigating `window.innerWidth` when that shot was taken. I've realized `--window-size=992,900` was specified, prompting further reflection.

**Revisiting Image Analysis**

I'm back to scrutinizing `w992.png`. Focusing on the overlaps now. I'm trying to identify the icon on the far left of the teal bar in the image. There was also a notable discrepancy with `blw` being 0px. I also need to look at `links` again. I wonder why `w992.png`...


**Analyzing the Overflow**

I've zeroed in on the `w992.png` scenario and the unexpected overflow. I've realized `blw`'s `width: 0` combined with visible overflow is the culprit. When the window is at 991px, the media queries cause `.navbar-links-wrapper` to have `width: 0` while the `.nav-link` elements are still `display: flex;`, causing them to overflow into the `navbar-menu-wrapper`, overlapping the dashboard elements. It explains why the icons are layered on top of Dashboard.


**Fixing the Overlap**

I've just uncovered a significant overlapping bug! I reviewed lines 410-415 of `_navbar.scss` and realized the solution. By setting `.navbar-links-wrapper` to `display: none;` (or similar bootstrap classes) at `max-width: 991px`, the overflow issue vanishes! At `>= 992px`, the width is properly set, and the display is normal. Now, to investigate how this plays out in sidebar-icon-only mode...


**Examining Sidebar Icons**

I'm now diving into the sidebar-icon-only mode, and I've reviewed the calculations for the `.navbar-breadcrumb`'s width with it active. I can confirm the `.navbar-links-wrapper` and `.navbar-menu-wrapper` are set to `78px` and `calc(100% - 78px)` respectively. It's working as expected. However, I've got a new puzzle: in tablet and mobile views, the navbar toggler and icons are getting pushed off the screen, and I'm off to `_navbar.scss` to understand why.


**Investigating Responsiveness**

I'm now zeroing in on the navbar's behavior at smaller screen sizes. The code excerpt focuses on the `navbar-menu-wrapper`'s width calculation. I noticed padding and width adjustments within a media query (max-width: 991px). I'm focusing on why the toggler and icons are getting pushed off-screen. Looking at `index.html`, I'm examining how the `navbar-menu-wrapper` is structured, specifically the `d-flex` and `justify-content-end` classes and the structure of the list items within.


**Analyzing Mobile Navbar**

I'm now examining how the navbar behaves on mobile, specifically the `navbar-brand-wrapper`. The key section in `_navbar.scss` shows a specific `width` declaration within a media query for smaller screens. I suspect this is where the culprit lies, as it could be affecting how the brand logo and toggler are rendered. I'm carefully reviewing the structure of the navbar items.


**Scrutinizing Width Calculations**

I'm now focusing on `.navbar-menu-wrapper` and its width calculation at smaller screen sizes. I see it's `calc(100% - 55px)` with padding. The items inside, like `nav-date` and the dropdowns, have specific `d-md-flex` and width constraints. I'm noting the hidden elements too. I'm reviewing the `navbar-toggler-right` and its padding. I want to be certain this all works responsively.

**Analyzing Mobile View Issue**

I'm now zeroing in on a critical issue with `mobile_view.png`. The `navbar-brand-wrapper` is inexplicably rendering as a purple box, obscuring content, specifically the email icon on the left side. It seems the visual cutoff stems from the purple box, and I need to pinpoint why it's there.


**Investigating Content Width**

I've uncovered that `mobile_view.png`'s issue stems from the page content exceeding the 375px image width, despite the Edge browser rendering a wider canvas. The `navbar`'s `fixed-top` and 100% width, in conjunction with the nested elements within `navbar-breadcrumb`, are causing the problem. The hidden `nav-search` isn't the culprit, but the content inside `Dashboard` and the breadcrumb are the root. I'm reviewing the SASS now, specifically the `nav-item` margins, to get to the solution.


**Examining Layout Discrepancies**

I'm now diving into the `index.html` layout, comparing it to the original design and other modern dashboards. The `navbar-breadcrumb`'s `ul.navbar-nav` with its `white-space: nowrap` or non-wrapping behavior seems problematic. Also, the charts within the `Transactions` card lack `width: 100%`, and the `d-flex` elements in `sales-chart-b` could be involved. I'm noting a typo (`mb-` instead of `mb-0`) potentially impacting visual presentation. I'm assessing how all this contributes to fixing the alignment issues.

   - Replaced legacy font families (`nunito-*`) with a modern system font stack (`"Segoe UI", system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif`) across all SCSS variables, compiled stylesheets (`style.css`), form inputs, buttons, and Chart.js runtime defaults.

parts.text:
**Analyzing Static Demos**

I've been examining the `.dropdown-menu-static-demo` class within the `_demo.scss` file. Specifically, I'm focusing on the `height` and `margin-bottom` properties. Additionally, the `z-index` of the `.dropdown-menu` is set to `0`. This is interesting because the position is `absolute` and `inset` is being used in Bootstrap 5.


**Investigating Further Alignment**

I've just pinpointed a critical alignment issue in the dropdown demo. When Popper isn't active, the default `top: 100%` setting is lost in Bootstrap 5. This causes the dropdown to overlap the button. However, the static demo neatly resolves this. I noticed setting `position: static; display: block; float: none; margin-top: 0.5rem;` does the trick! Now, I am exploring other pages for similar potential alignment overlaps.

**Analyzing Visual Discrepancies**

I've been looking at the screenshots, and a few visual problems are apparent. The logo and profile images are broken. "Eugenia Mullins Last login was 23 hours ago" is run together. Finally, I've noted the current Poppins font family and the `#f4f5fa` background color for future reference.


**Adjusting Visual Elements**

I'm now diving into the SCSS files to address the visual issues I identified. Specifically, I'm focusing on `_variables.scss` to change the background and font, making the text more readable. I'm also working in `_navbar.scss` to ensure the menu behaves responsively across different screen sizes, and I'm addressing the layout issues in the `.main-panel` within `_vertical-wrapper.scss` to improve the overall look.


**Refining Style Consistency**

I'm now zeroing in on style refinements across various SCSS and CSS files. I'm focusing on the `_demo.scss` file, specifically the `.doughnut-chart-sm` and `.dropdown-menu-static-demo` components, to ensure proper sizing and display. I'm also updating typography in `_typography.scss` and making further style adjustments to the footer's background and font family in `_footer.scss`. Finally, I'm compiling and implementing those changes into the `style.css` and `dist/assets/css/style.css` files.


**Correcting Image Paths**

I'm now focused on rectifying broken image links within both `index.html` files. I'm updating file paths to ensure the logo, mini-logo, profile images, and documentation link correctly point to their assets. Additionally, I'm cleaning up typos like the "mb-" and "daoughnut" mistakes. I'm also ensuring the profile card and footer text aligns nicely, and then making grid column adjustments.

The background color, layout overlapping alignment issues, and font family have been updated across the PolluxUI webapp:

- **Background Color**: Configured a modern `#edf2f8` theme across the application body, scroller containers, and content wrappers with clean `#ffffff` card elevations.
- **Layout & Alignment Overlaps**: Resolved the mobile/tablet breadcrumb icons overlapping the dashboard title, corrected the 8px main panel horizontal overflow, added proper spacing/dividers between user profile and status, fixed overlapping dropdown menus in demo components, corrected responsive card column wrapping at medium/large breakpoints, fixed Chart.js rendering constraints, and restored broken relative image paths.
- **Typography**: Updated font family across stylesheets and SCSS variables to `"Segoe UI", system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`.
